                           Recipe used in "Effects of microstructure on the sky-green color in imitating ancient
                        Jun glazes"
                             Jianfeng ZHU,3 Pei SHI,33 Fen WANG, Longlong DONG and Ting ZHAO
                           School of Materials Science and Engineering, Shaanxi University of Science &
                            Technology, Xi’an 710021, China

                                                                                                  Images from article
                               “The sky-green glaze of ancient Jun ware was successfully imitated with
                                   the addition of 4 wt % calcium phosphate for introducing the phosphorus                   Derek Au                                                                                                                              5 years ago
                                      (P) to the composition. Effects of the calcium phosphate contents on the
                                      chromaticity, precipitated phase and microstructure of sky-green glaze
                               were investigated. Based on the analysis of colorimeter, XRD, FT-IR, XPS
                              and SEM, a possible coloring mechanism was proposed to explain the
                                        variation of glaze colors with the increasing of calcium phosphate
                                     content. The results indicated that the addition of calcium phosphate
                                    contributed to increasing the content of calcium iron phosphate
                                 [Ca19Fe2(PO4)14] and the size of phase separation droplets in glazes.
                              The formation of Ca19Fe2(PO4)14 decreased the ratio of Fe2+ to Fe3+
                              and the increased size of phase separation droplets weakened the
                                       structural color, which increased the L* and b* value of glazes. Therefore,
                                   the color of sky-green glaze got more green and white gradually.”

                                                                                                                       Hubert Vezier
                                                                                                         5 years ago

Thank you for all these shared documents.
                                                                                                                                I started from the chemical composition of the old Jun that
                                                              you published and I used the raw materials that I find in
                                                                      France. I baked in a gas oven with a slight reduction to C7
                                                            and the result is quite consistent with Jun.
                                                                                                                                I am very happy with the result.
                                                             Thank you



                                                                            Drew King
                                                                           5 days ago

                                                                                                                                I noticed that this recipe uses a soda feldspar despite all
                                                                                  original compositions and recreations using a potash feldspar
                                                                          -- are there any resources that detail how using a soda
                                                                          feldspar might impact results? I've only gotten good, vibrant
                                                                              results with a soda feldspar myself. The best I can think of is
                                                                            that a soda feldspar would impact dripping and crazing, but
                                                                          I'm unsure on how it would impact color and elements like
                                                                                   liquid-liquid phase separation.
